bull_bear.body:
- integration: design-to-production model combining engineering, tool-room capability, stamping, welding and assembly — evidence: in-house tool room and design centres support product engineering, re-engineering, sheet-metal design, reverse engineering, tooling development and prototyping
- customer lock-in: deepening participation across OEM platforms reduces customer/programme concentration risk — evidence: supplied components and assemblies across 25 vehicle variants in FY26, up from 5 variants in 2022
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Energy Management & Transition — Energy is a significant operating input across the manufacturing footprint; price volatility, grid constraints or supply interruptions may affect cost competitiveness and operational continuity.
- Employee Health and Safety — Manufacturing operations involve shop-floor, equipment and process-related risks; a serious safety incident may affect employee well-being, productivity, continuity and reputation.
- Product Life Cycle Management — Changing customer requirements, model cycles and technology transitions can affect product demand, utilisation and returns on programme-specific investment.
- Supply Chain Sustainability and Reporting — Supplier non-compliance, capacity constraints, quality issues or disruptions can affect production continuity, customer delivery and responsible-sourcing expectations.
- Data Privacy — Increasing digitalisation and handling of customer, employee and business information create exposure to unauthorised access, cyber incidents and data loss.
- Human Rights and Labour Practices — Manufacturing and extended supply chains require continued attention to labour standards, workplace practices, inclusion and responsible sourcing; non-compliance may lead to regulatory, operational and reputational consequences.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company designs, tools and manufactures sheet-metal components, sub-assemblies, structural assemblies and tubular products for passenger vehicles, SUVs, commercial vehicles and other mobility applications. Its core business divisions span engineering/design services, a tool room (press-tool design, manufacturing, jigs & fixtures), medium and large stamped mechanical assemblies (floor/door assemblies, load bodies, cross beams, exhaust systems, tubular assemblies) and mechanical assemblies (pedal control systems, parking brakes, door hinges, jack assemblies, cab stay and cab tilt). It also evaluates capability-adjacent, non-automotive opportunities such as solar structures, construction equipment and railways.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Concept, Style, Design, Analysis & Engineering Services:** Automotive engineering services for product design, development and validation
- **Tool Room:** Press tool design and formability analysis, Press tool manufacturing, jigs & fixtures, Tool try-outs
- **Medium and Large Stamped Mechanical Assemblies:** Complete floor and door assemblies, Sub assemblies, Load bodies and cross beams, Exhaust systems, Tubular assemblies and sheet metal stampings
- **Mechanical Assemblies:** Pedal control system, Parking brake, Door hinges, jack assemblies, Cab stay and cab tilt
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Autoline Design Software Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned; Group's engineering and product development arm — supports OEM customers through integrated engineering services (product engineering, BIW design, reverse engineering, rapid prototyping). Subject to a Board-approved Scheme of Amalgamation into the parent.
- Autoline E-Mobility Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% owned; builds the Group's electric mobility platform — electric two-wheeler ecosystem including product, battery-related and distribution initiatives; targeting dealer-network expansion across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka.
- Koderat Investments Limited (Cyprus) — subsidiary: 100% owned Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) incorporated in Cyprus; no business activities. Previously held 49% of Italian companies SZ Design Srl (declared bankrupt, investment impaired to Nil) and Zagato Srl (voluntarily liquidated; Koderat excluded as shareholder).
- Autoline Industrial Parks Limited — related party: Company divested its entire shareholding; ceased to be a subsidiary with effect from April 15, 2025.
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- integration: design-to-production model combining engineering, tool-room capability, stamping, welding and assembly — evidence: in-house tool room and design centres support product engineering, re-engineering, sheet-metal design, reverse engineering, tooling development and prototyping
- customer lock-in: deepening participation across OEM platforms reduces customer/programme concentration risk — evidence: supplied components and assemblies across 25 vehicle variants in FY26, up from 5 variants in 2022
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Deepen existing OEM partnerships (Tata Motors, Mahindra, Ashok Leyland) while selectively pursuing new customer acquisitions
- Diversify into capability-adjacent non-automotive segments (solar trackers/structures, base structures, aluminium extrusions, railways, formwork, construction equipment)
- Develop EV-focused components and systems for the electric vehicle market
- Improve capacity utilisation and selectively augment press, welding and related manufacturing infrastructure, governed by customer visibility and execution readiness
- Drive productivity and operating leverage through automation, robotic welding/press lines and Industry 4.0 / ERP (SAP S/4HANA) digital integration
- Shift strategic emphasis from revenue growth alone to margin quality — business mix, material productivity, contribution margins, plant-level cost discipline
- Maintain capital discipline — receivables, inventory optimisation, tooling recovery and reduction of financial-cost intensity
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 centred on the continued ramp-up of the Sanand (Gujarat) manufacturing facility, which supports passenger-vehicle programmes and future capacity requirements, alongside robotic press operations, welding automation and Industry 4.0-oriented initiatives at existing units. The Directors' Report describes a capacity strategy built on deployment of hydraulic presses, robotic welding solutions and other automation-led interventions, with capital deployment increasingly linked to customer programme visibility, commissioning milestones, utilisation and expected financial returns. Looking to FY27, capacity creation is described as continuing to be selectively augmented (press, welding and related manufacturing infrastructure) and governed by customer visibility, execution readiness, capital discipline and expected returns; the Company also flags selective development of capability-adjacent non-automotive opportunities (solar structures, formwork, industrial applications).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's infrastructure-led growth, localisation agenda and manufacturing incentives (PLI, PM E-DRIVE, SPMEPCI) create a favourable backdrop for customer-backed capacity creation
- Electrification, premiumisation, smartification and safety requirements are increasing engineering content and component value, favouring integrated engineering/tooling/manufacturing capability
- Growth expected to remain customer-backed and execution-led, anchored in deeper OEM participation, selective customer diversification and increased content across new vehicle platforms
- Passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle programme ramp-ups, tooling revenues and improved product mix are cited as demand drivers
- Raw-material/commodity-price volatility, programme concentration, changing propulsion technologies and global trade disruptions are flagged as offsetting factors requiring disciplined capacity planning
- Chairman's letter cites 'a strong order book, diversified customer portfolio, an expanding programme base' supporting a platform for sustained and profitable growth
- Directors' Report cites a 'healthy order pipeline' and increasing business opportunities from existing and new customers as supporting future growth prospects
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
